instruction: Enable high contrast mode to make the interface more visible.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: GTK_THEME=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 2>/dev/null | tr -d "'"); if echo "$GTK_THEME" | grep -qi 'high\|contrast'; then echo "High contrast enabled (theme: $GTK_THEME)"; else echo "No high contrast enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: This task requires enabling high contrast mode. The evaluator checks if a high-contrast GTK theme is enabled by examining the org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme setting. High contrast themes typically have 'high' or 'contrast' in their name (e.g., HighContrast, HighContrastInverse). The task is similar in difficulty to the original - both require navigating accessibility settings and enabling a single option. No custom functions needed as we use existing check_include_exclude metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts system state by querying the GTK theme setting (org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme)
Verification logic is semantically appropriate - high contrast themes in GNOME/Ubuntu do contain 'high' or 'contrast' in their name (e.g., HighContrast, HighContrastInverse)
Metric function (check_include_exclude) correctly handles type='rule' pattern - receives rules dict directly as expected parameter
Complete coverage - verifies the single requirement (high contrast mode enabled)
Proper error handling with timeout and stderr redirection, plus 'error' in exclude list
Case-insensitive matching (grep -qi) is appropriate for theme name checking
No postconfig needed - system settings persist after being changed
